newsitem.title: USA: Calif. commissioner seizes Golden Eagle Insurance.
newsitem.headline: Calif. commissioner seizes Golden Eagle Insurance.

text.p: California's insurance commissioner said on Friday he served a court order to take over control and operation of Golden Eagle Insurance Co, one of the largest writers of workers' compensation insurance in the state.

"Certain business practices by the management of Golden Eagle Insurance Co have put both the company and consumers at risk," said California Insurance Commissioner Chuck Quackenbush. "This court-ordered takeover is necessary to ensure that policyholder claims will be paid."

The Superior Court of San Diego County gave the Department of Insurance the authority to immediately seize the company, all its assets, books and records. The court decision allows the department to operate the company as an appointed conservator, Quackenbush said in a statement.

Last September, California's insurance commissioner issued an order directing San Diego-based Golden Eagle Insurance, which is privately-held, to increase its reserves by $138.5 million. The order followed an Insurance Department examination of the company, state officials said.
"We obtained evidence that there was substantial manipulation of the data to cover up the $138.5 million shortfall," Quackenbush said.

"In light of this manipulation of data, and Golden Eagle's refusal to provide all of the audited financial statements, the only prudent course of action was to take over the company to protect California consumers," he added.

Quackenbush said consumers and clients of Golden Eagle should not be affected by the take over. "Claims will be paid and the company will continue to compete for its fair share of the marketplace," he said.
